findings.description: A 7th column, 'Quote Date' (index 12), is written as a live Formula — `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — but SHEET-FORMULA-001's parenthetical enumerates exactly six live-price-dependent columns (price, market value, unrealized P&L, unrealized %, estimated unrealized tax, net unrealized). Quote Date is not one of them, so under the spec's own closing clause ('all other columns as engine-written values') it should literally be a Value, not a Formula — the code's real reason (the marks read-back needs GOOGLEFINANCE's own quote date, locale-proofed, per the design doc's SHEET-MARK-* family) is invisible from SHEET-FORMULA-001 alone. All three B-runs independently reconstruct this exact column, its formula text, and its index (12); the `positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column` test pins it. None of the three A-runs produce anything like it — nothing in the given spec text hints such a column exists, so it can't be an A-side omission, only a pure B-side surplus.

The Est. Tax Rate `Cell::Value` must be serialized as a Sheets `userEnteredValue` (never a forced `stringValue`), so a literal like "20.0000%" coerces to the numeric fraction 0.20 that `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)` can multiply as a number rather than inert text — pinned by a dedicated test (`est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`) and an explicit doc-comment contract on `batch_update_view` ('Value typing' / 'Formula typing'). SHEET-FORMULA-001 says nothing about Sheets-API cell serialization/typing — its value-vs-formula split is purely about which columns get which content, not how either is written. All three B-runs capture this in detail (B2 gives it two dedicated bullets, including that a `Cell::Formula` must ALSO be a `userEnteredValue`); none of the three A-runs touch Sheets-API value-typing at all — it's structurally out of scope for all three (no client trait, no serialization layer in any A sketch).

Row-anchoring and layout constants are pinned but absent from the spec text: `DATA_START_ROW = 2` (row 1 is a frozen header, never rewritten), and every row-anchored formula (Market Value, Unrealized P&L, etc.) must reference ONLY its own row — the test `per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header` explicitly asserts a formula string does NOT contain any OTHER row's cell coordinate ('so a row shift cannot mis-pair the cells'). SHEET-FORMULA-001 only distinguishes value vs. formula columns; it says nothing about row layout, frozen headers, or cross-row reference safety. All three B-runs reconstruct the constant and the no-cross-row-reference rule near-verbatim; the three A-runs each invent a different, mutually incompatible column/row layout scheme (A1 fixes an enum-derived A1 letter order matching the EARS list order; A2/A3 take column letters as an opaque caller-supplied parameter) since the spec gives zero layout guidance — this weakens A-run comparability but isn't itself an A-side finding (nothing in the spec text is being contradicted, just left open).

`render_positions` returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` if two `Snapshot.positions` entries share a symbol — a defensive assertion the code's own comment calls 'structurally UNREACHABLE through the real API' (Map-keyed by symbol) but kept so 'a future non-Map source cannot silently double-render a symbol.' SHEET-FORMULA-001 is entirely silent on duplicate-row handling — this belongs to the row-identity invariant the read-back depends on, not the value/formula boundary. All three B-runs document the error path, though with different fidelity to the code's own 'defensive/unreachable' framing: B3 preserves it almost verbatim ('defensive, structurally unreachable via the real Map-backed API, kept for a future non-Map source'), B1 gestures at it ('row-identity invariant the formula anchoring depends on'), B2 states it as a flat, unqualified requirement with no unreachability caveat. None of the three A-runs have any concept of a duplicate-row error since nothing in the given EARS text suggests one is needed.

Exact formula algebra is pinned by code/tests but nowhere in the spec text: `Price = =GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","price")` (explicit "price" attribute), `Market Value = =E{r}*B{r}`, `Unrealized P&L = =F{r}-D{r}`, `Est. Unrealized Tax = =G{r}*H{r}`, `Net Unrealized = =G{r}*(1-H{r})` (computed directly as PnL×(1-rate), not as a subtraction against a separately materialized tax cell), `Unrealized % = =IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`. Notably the real tax/net formulas apply symmetrically to losses — a negative Unrealized P&L produces a negative 'Est. Unrealized Tax' (a tax benefit), with no floor at zero — a semantic choice SHEET-FORMULA-001 never addresses. This is the sharpest illustration of the audit's blind spot: all three independent A-runs, forced to invent an answer to a question the spec never poses, unanimously gated the tax term at `MAX(0, PnL)` (losses get zero estimated tax) — the opposite of what the real formula does. Per the classification rules this unanimous A-side invention has no basis in spec text and isn't itself a countable A-finding, but the divergence from the real (B-pinned) behavior is real and uncaught by SHEET-FORMULA-001 in either direction.

Whether the Open Lots and Realized tabs' 'every cell is a Value' behavior is actually test-pinned is itself unstable across the B-runs: B1 explicitly flags it as untested ('code shows all-Value, no test asserts it' — only the Tax tab has a dedicated `tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula` test), while B2 and B3 state it as a flat, unqualified 'SHALL' requirement with the same weight as the tested Tax-tab claim. Checked against `formula.rs`: B1 is correct — there is no test covering Open Lots/Realized's formula-vs-value split, only source code (`render_open_lots`/`render_realized` construct exclusively `Cell::Value`). This is a minor provenance-accuracy gap between the B-runs rather than a spec/code drift per se.

notes: Real EARS text (SHEET-FORMULA-001) is a single terse sentence naming exactly six formula columns; the real code+tests carry substantially more structure (a 7th formula column for the marks read-back, a Sheets-API serialization contract, row-anchoring/layout constants, a defensive duplicate-row error, and exact formula algebra including a symmetric-loss tax treatment) that the given spec text never states. Direction A produced no material finding: everything the three A-runs invented either matches the code's shape at the level the spec actually constrains (six columns, value/formula split, zero-basis guard) or is unanimous invention with zero spec-text basis (units, tax-rate injection mechanism, GOOGLEFINANCE argument form, MAX(0,·) tax floor) — per protocol these don't count as A-findings even where they diverge from the real code. Direction B surfaced multiple well-corroborated, code-pinned behaviors invisible from SHEET-FORMULA-001's text alone. Net: B-ONLY-DRIFT. A-run agreement is high on the primary classification (which six columns are formulas) but only medium once you look at formula mechanics (units, tax-rate mechanism, GOOGLEFINANCE signature all diverge pairwise). B-run agreement is high throughout, with one accuracy nuance (B1 correctly flags Open Lots/Realized's all-Value split as untested; B2/B3 state it as flatly pinned).
